mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-frequency rate spikes (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market softness offsets inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined labor-inflation signal (Pearson IC > 0.2), or unemployment claims do not rise while CPIAUCSL declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month's level precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return by signaling robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite INDPRO exceeding the 2% threshold (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as weak building activity indicates softening demand for capital goods and consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the 3-month HOUST decline does not precede returns (lagged IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in a quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to improved labor market conditions and reduced policy tightening expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a given quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat despite the UNRATE crossing below 4% (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer demand indicators (GDPC1) over the prior 2 months predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as dual labor and demand strength supports optimism.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and GDPC1 increase over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC < 0.15) when both proxies trend up together.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the monthly RSAFS (reserves) series of over 10% suggests excess liquidity in the financial system, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return via equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month decline > 10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive during the liquidity decline (IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price inflation index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to immediate market concern about wage-price spirals.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such CPIAUCSL spikes (IC > 0.1).
